stem.text: Hydrogen and iodine can react reversibly to produce hydrogen iodide. The equation is shown.

$4.00\,\text{mol}$ of hydrogen gas and $X\,\text{mol}$ of iodine vapour are mixed in a sealed container of volume $1.00\,\text{dm}^{3}$ at a temperature of $460\,\text{K}$. The system is allowed to reach equilibrium.
The equilibrium mixture contains $2.00\,\text{mol}$ of hydrogen iodide. The equilibrium constant, $K_\text{c}$, for the reaction at $460\,\text{K}$ is $4.0$.
